triage.words: above the non-spinning (mu = 0) line: unlikely to have dropped 50 g or more
below the spinning-body (mu = 2/3) line: a likely meteorite dropper

outcome.headline: Winchcombe: the fireball's own flight says it dropped meteorites (likely by alpha-beta), the simulated fall line runs within 563 m of all 10 stones found, and the orbit before it met the Earth matches the published one to 0.4 sigma.
outcome.action: Search along the fall line, heavier stones further along the track; download the strewn field (GeoJSON or KML).

checked_against.name: perihelion distance q (AU)
checked_against.source: McMullan et al. 2023 (orbit); Russell et al. 2024 (find sites)

outcome.confidence: across the track every find within 563 m of the simulated stones; along it, 5 of 10 where stones released at the luminous end land, 9 of 10 allowing release anywhere after the last flare (34.9 km)
limits: not reproduced along the track: 20.6 g at Winchcombe
